description: GraphQL engine fingerprint signatures. Patterns are matched (case-insensitively) against the concatenated text of all probe responses (status line, headers, and body). The first engine whose required patterns all match wins; ties are broken by declaration order (most specific engines listed first). Derived from graphw00f (dolevf) and the GraphQL Threat Matrix (nicholasess).

engines.name: hasura
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Exposes full Postgres schema via introspection unless permissions are explicitly restricted per role
Anonymous role, if enabled, can leak schema and data without authentication
Admin secret leakage grants full database access

engines.name: wpgraphql
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Exposes WordPress object types including the users connection by default, enabling user enumeration
Public schema introspection enabled by default in many installs
Plugin/theme versions may be inferable from exposed types

engines.name: apollo
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Introspection disabled in production (NODE_ENV=production) since v3, but frequently re-enabled by operators
Field suggestions ('Did you mean') enabled by default, leaking schema even when introspection is off
APQ (automatic persisted queries) may allow unauthenticated cache population
CSRF prevention is opt-in (csrfPrevention) and off in older configurations

engines.name: graphene
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Introspection enabled by default, not gated on environment
Field suggestions enabled by default, leaking schema names
No built-in query depth or complexity limiting

engines.name: strawberry
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Introspection and GraphiQL enabled by default in the development server
No default query depth or complexity limiting

engines.name: yoga

any: unable to parse request body as json

known_default_insecure_behaviors: GraphiQL enabled by default; introspection enabled by default
Field suggestions enabled by default via graphql-js
APQ supported via plugin and may be unprotected

engines.name: mercurius
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Introspection enabled by default
GraphiQL/JIT may expose schema details
No default depth limiting (queryDepth plugin is opt-in)

engines.name: graphql-ruby
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Introspection enabled by default unless disable_introspection_entry_points is set
Field suggestions ('Did you mean') enabled by default
Max depth/complexity limits are opt-in

engines.name: graphql-js
known_default_insecure_behaviors: Introspection enabled by default
Field suggestions ('Did you mean') enabled by default, leaking schema even when introspection is disabled
No default query depth or complexity limiting
